Geometrically, it equals the product of their lengths and the cosine of the angle between them."},{"type":"ui","source":"protocol source","state":[{"name":"lengthA","value":3},{"name":"lengthB","value":4},{"name":"angleDegrees","value":60}]},{"type":"text","text":"If we have vectors A and B with lengths |A| and |B| and angle θ between them, then: dot(A,B) = |A| × |B| × cos(θ)."},{"type":"ui","source":"initial state","state":[{"name":"angleDegrees","value":60}]},{"type":"text","text":"When the vectors are orthogonal (at 90°), cos(90°) = 0, so their dot product is zero. This means they have no component in common direction."},{"type":"text","text":"If the angle is greater than 90°, the cosine is negative, so the dot product is negative. This corresponds to a negative projection of one vector onto the other."},{"type":"ui","source":"vector visualization","state":[{"name":"lengthA","value":3},{"name":"lengthB","value":4},{"name":"angleDegrees","value":120}]},{"type":"text","text":"The dot product can be seen as the length of one vector times the projection of the other vector onto it. The sign indicates the direction of the projection: positive if they point roughly the same way, zero if perpendicular, and negative if pointing opposite."}]}
